result.rationale: In the hubspot CalendarService diff, refreshOAuthTokens returns either the hubspot SDK result (normal path) or a raw fetch Response (credential-sync path: `return response;` from a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`). The result is typed as HubspotToken and used directly (`hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in`, `setAccessToken(...)`), so in sync mode the values are from a Response object, producing undefined/NaN expiryDate and an undefined access token. Verifiable from the diff and a real correctness defect, though conditional on sync being enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. That `Response` is not parsed and will not have HubSpot token fields (e.g., `accessToken` / expiry fields), so subsequent logic that computes expiry or sets the access token will receive `undefined`, leading to `NaN` expiry calculations and an unauthenticated client path. This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff and is a real runtime defect when the sync feature is enabled.
